sweep_summary: Yine (yine1238) is in the catalog as fixed-strict penultimate (StressTyp2 paraphrase of Matteson 1965:21 plus Hanson 2010 sec. 2.4). The search of works with stress or accent in the title has a single item, Parker 1989 'Un análisis métrico del acento en el piro' (ILV Peru Documento de Trabajo 21:114-125), already listed in our bibliography and the only work devoted specifically to Piro/Yine stress. I located its current SIL archive records (entry 30280 for the article, 29888 for the volume; the Glottolog URL with id 23438 is dead and that number now points to an unrelated item) and found that the whole volume is offered as an open PDF (5.75 MB) on entry 29888, but the file sits behind an automated-access block that our network cannot pass (403 loop by automated download, curl_cffi, cloudscraper, headless and headed Chrome with the Turnstile checkbox clicked); an Internet Archive copy exists but web.archive.org is could not be reached by automated download. So Parker 1989 remains unread: access unknown-from-here, priority high (it should settle how the secondary/tertiary alternating pattern in the rule string is to be stated, which Hanson 2010 calls variable; primary penultimate stress is not in doubt). The only text newly read this search of works with stress in the title is Easterday 2019 (open LangSci book, Appendix B p. 491), a secondary compilation that codes Yine as 'Word stress: Yes; Stress placement: Fixed; correlates: pitch (impressionistic)' - consistent with the classification but not a first-hand placement statement, so no new stress statement was found and the catalog's deciding source is unchanged. Records saved and logged in (, +). Recommended follow-up: download from the SIL URL above in an ordinary browser (it is openly downloadable) and read pp. 114-125.org APIs.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.deciding_source_kind: database or survey citing another work
audit.reasoning: Coding: fixed-strict, penultimate primary, stress placement coded per word length as 10 010 1010 10010 101010 1010010 10101010 (1 = a stressed syllable) (primary penult; secondary initial; further stresses on odd syllables except the one before the penult). (1) The record carries no quotation of its own; the StressTyp2 passage it rests on is confirmed in, and the Hanson 2010 passage in the the domain quotation field is verbatim at sec. 2.4 pp. 36-37 of the copy we hold. Matteson 1965:21 itself is not yet obtained. (2) The deciding source is a database paraphrase of the 1965 reference grammar. Against Glottolog's list (Matteson 1965 and Hanson 2010 are the two grammars; the phonology items Lin 1997/2005 and Zimmermann 2013 are on syllable/mora structure and vowel deletion, not stress) the best first-hand descriptions are Matteson (1954/1965) and Hanson 2010, plus Parker 1989 as the one dedicated stress paper. (3) downloaded now: Matteson 1954 (open Rosetta excerpt) state

sources.quote: "Primary stress of words occurs on the penultimate syllable, and secondary stress on the first syllable. In words with an even number of syllables a slight stress occurs on all odd-numbered syllables. In words with an odd number of syllables a slight stress occurs on all odd-numbered syllables except the one immediately preceding the primary-stressed penultimate syllable. ... However, in calling and exclamation the stress may be moved to the final syllable with raise of pitch and lengthening of the final vowel."
